# 4 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Praise of Eleazar

---

**1** O blessed old age! O venerable white hair! O life lived faithfully by the law and sealed with the honor of martyrdom!

**2** If Eleazar had given way even briefly and saved himself, people would have said that devotion in old age is just a matter of self-preservation.

**3** But he made old age truly honored — not by saving himself but by dying faithful.

**4** He proved that in those who are truly devoted to God, old age is beautiful — not diminished by danger but crowned by it.

**5** Which is more wonderful — that reason conquered the passions in this man, or that the law itself, working through him, achieved this victory?

**6** Eleazar the priest, ninety years old, his body frail, his flesh consumed by torment — through the power of holy reason he proved that reason is master over the passions.

**7** You triumphed over the tyrant through the strength of your reasoning and overcame every pain his torturers could inflict!

**8** Just as Aaron our ancestor seized the incense burner and ran through the flaming congregation, stopping the destroying angel by the power of prayer,

**9** so Eleazar, consumed in fire, proved by his willingness to die that reason empowered by devotion can extinguish any passion.

**10** And this too was admirable: though his body was broken by age and his strength had faded, he renewed his youthful courage through reason and neutralized the power of the rack.

**11** O noble father! O great elder! O holy keeper of the law! You did not flinch before the torture instruments!

**12** You were not broken by the whip! You were not conquered by the burning!

**13** You remained devoted to God's holy name and faithful in piety until your last breath!

**14** O true priest of God, faithful guardian of the sacred law, devoted protector of religious life!

**15** While your body was being consumed by fire, your soul clung to the holy purpose of the law.

**16** Your courage and self-mastery proved beyond any doubt that reason can govern the passions.

**17** Even your enemies were in awe, watching you endure the torments without yielding.

**18** Even the tyrant and his whole court were astonished by your endurance.

**19** And this brought no small honor to your people and to the divine law.

**20** After Eleazar died, the seven brothers were brought before the tyrant alongside their mother to face the same test.

**21** These brothers had been raised in the same law and shaped by the same devotion, and they were in every way worthy of the noble old priest.

**22** Their mother, seeing them all and rejoicing in the brave spirit in them, spoke to them in their ancestral language: My children, the contest is noble. God summons you to it as witnesses for our nation. Fight for the law of your fathers with all your heart.

**23** She added: It would make no sense for me — the one who made you love your own lives — to be destroyed by grief over your deaths.
